old: Dilution. Shares went from 27.3M at FY2022 to 41.4M at Q2 FY2026 through equity raises, stock-paid acquisitions (Bridg: 1.81M shares) and stock compensation that runs at 6.0% of revenue. The 4% 2031 notes convert at $19.02 into 13.9M shares, 34% of today's count, so above that price most of the upside is shared with noteholders; the base target already uses 57.2M shares. Another raise or convertible at these prices would cut per-share value further.

Share loss to Toast and AI-native tools. Toast has $6.8B of LTM revenue against PAR's $0.5B (FiscalAI) and is moving from independents into chains. In Q2 FY2026 PAR's organic unique active sites fell 2.6% YoY to 145,900, explained by planned Punchh exits at ~80% discounts. If that proves to be the start of loyalty customers leaving rather than a one-off clean-up, ARR growth drops toward the 8% of the bear case, worth $8.04 per share against $27.60 in the base.

Concentration in a few large customers. McDonald's alone was 21% of FY2025 revenue (FiscalAI KPI), mostly hardware and services at ~20-25% gross margin, and H2 FY2026 ARR growth depends on the Burger King and Papa John's rollouts. A pause at one Tier-1 account moves revenue and ARR by more than a quarter's worth of new logos: H2 FY2025 net ARR adds were ~$30M in total.

Payments pricing competition. Fintech gross profit is $1,282M of the $2,082M LTM recurring gross profit (62%), and it depends on a take rate of ~0.60% of GPV. Square, Clover (Fiserv), Shift4/SkyTab and SpotOn sell to the same small restaurants and compete mainly on processing price and bundled lending; in September 2026 an Atlanta restaurant publicly switched to SpotOn citing ~40% cheaper financing than Toast Capital. Each 1bp of take rate is ~$21M of gross profit on LTM GPV of $214.9B, and 5bps (back to the 0.55% seen in FY2023–FY2024) would remove ~$107M, about a quarter of LTM GAAP operating income.

Hardware cost and inventory. Every new location is won with hardware sold below cost: hardware and professional services gross profit was -$259M LTM (-12.4% of recurring gross profit). Memory prices have risen sharply; Toast built inventory to $217M (from $103M a year earlier) to secure supply, which cut 2Q FY2026 FCF to $130M from $208M, and the CFO expects a larger P&L hit in FY2027 than in FY2026. If the hardware loss widens to ~15% of recurring gross profit, the margin expansion in the base case is delayed by roughly a year.

Credit risk in Toast Capital and restaurant failures. Non-payments fintech (led by Toast Capital merchant cash advances) contributed $57M of gross profit in 2Q FY2026 (9bps of take rate), and opex that quarter included $29M of bad debt and credit-related expenses. Restaurants are small, thin-margin businesses with high failure rates; a consumer slowdown would hit GPV per location (flat yoy in 2Q FY2026), lending losses and location churn at the same time. FiscalAI does not break out loan balances or loss rates, so this exposure is not measured in the model.

Generative AI substitutes the content in Health and Legal. Health (€1,596M) and Legal & Regulatory (€1,005M) were 42% of FY2025 revenue, and both sell curated expert content that large language models can approximate for simple questions. UpToDate Pro, the individual-clinician product, is already competing with free medical chatbots (under 2% of group revenue), OpenEvidence is growing fast in U.S. clinical search, and Harvey and Legora (combined ARR above $400M per BNP Paribas) are scaling in legal workflow. The company has not disclosed retention, pricing or usage to rebut it. If organic growth halves to 2.5% and the multiple stays at 11x, the bear case gives €63 per share, 7% below today.

Capital return is capped by distributable reserves, not by cash. After €4,096M of buybacks in FY2022–FY2025 at €84–€181 per share, equity is €940M and the 2026 buyback had to be cut to €500M from €1,096M. The company is returning ~100% of free cash flow, but less of it can go to buybacks exactly when the shares are cheapest (12.5x adjusted EPS), and a new CEO (Stacey Caywood, first year in the role) is raising product development to 12–13% of revenue and doing bolt-on M&A (Marosa, StandardFusion, Libra). If reserves stay tight, the per-share compounding in the base case (208M diluted shares by FY2029) slows.

Dollar and U.S. macro exposure. North America was 64% of H1 2026 revenue; the weaker dollar cut reported revenue by 5% (€148M) in H1 2026 even as organic growth was 5%. Transactional revenue in Financial & Corporate Compliance (€169M in H1 2026) depends on U.S. mortgage and M&A volumes, which stayed subdued without the rate cut management had expected. Hypothesis (not a company figure): with over 60% of adjusted operating profit earned in North America, a further 5-cent fall in the dollar would take roughly 2–3% off euro-reported EPS without any change in the business.

Management said on the Q2 FY2026 call that H2 ARR net adds will exceed the ~$30M of H2 FY2025, taking organic growth from 12.3% to "a higher percent in the teens" in Q3 and Q4, driven by Burger King (400+ sites a month) and the start of Papa John's.

Q3 FY2026 (reported around 5 November 2026) is the first test. If organic growth stays near 12%, the base case's 12% a year to FY2029 has no cushion and the site-count decline of Q2 FY2026 starts to look like more than the one-off Punchh exits.

PAR Intelligence was live at ~20,000 sites at the end of Q2 FY2026, with another 20,000 planned for Q3 and a commitment of 50,000 for FY2026. Management expects 2027 to be the year AI contributes to revenue, most likely as a subscription add-on to back office and loyalty.

This is the answer to the market's AI question: if PAR can charge for it, the platform gains from AI instead of being displaced by it. The bull case depends on it; the base does not.

Management said in Q2 FY2026 that three Tier-1 RFPs remain open (one global, per the analyst question), with more at an early stage, and excludes them from its mid-teens ARR target. A Tier-1 win of ~10,000-15,000 sites is roughly the difference between the base and the bull on site count.

A signed deal also matters for the margin of safety: it is the event most likely to move the stock above the $19.02 conversion price of the 2031 notes.

Guidance for Q3 FY2026 is $615–625M of non-GAAP recurring gross profit (+22–24%) and $210–220M of adjusted EBITDA. Net adds were ~7,500 in Q3 FY2025, ~7,000 in Q1 FY2026 and a record 9,500 in Q2 FY2026. Holding 8,000+ in a seasonally average quarter would confirm the base case path of ~31K net adds a year and that Q2 was not a one-off pulled forward by the World Cup and a large chain win (Kung Fu Tea, 300+ locations).

Results expected on or around 3 November 2026.

Management said on the 2Q FY2026 call that ARR in the new TAMs is "on a path to nearly double ARR to $200 million this year" and that each is scaling faster than the core did at the same stage. That is ~8% of the $2.41B total ARR. Reaching it would support the bull case's location and ARPU assumptions (fuel payments, grocery, hotels via Best Western, stadiums). Missing it while spending continues would make the new-market investment the main drag on margins.

Clinical Solutions (UpToDate, Medi-Span, about 59% of Health and roughly 15% of group revenue) grew 6% organically in H1 2025 and 5% in H1 2026. Management attributes the slowdown to a Medi-Span one-off in Q1 2025, while BNP Paribas cited third-party data showing UpToDate weekly active users falling since May 2026 and OpenEvidence traffic rising. Expert AI is bundled into Enterprise renewals, so AI substitution would show up first as slower renewal pricing here. A print below 4% would be the first reported evidence that the content moat is leaking, and would break claim 1.

North American cloud software revenue grew 18% organically in H1 2026 as firms migrate from ProSystem fx to CCH Axcess (just past the halfway mark) and ~250 firms subscribed to the new agentic AI modules. Tax & Accounting is the largest division (€1,660M, 27% of FY2025 revenue) and guides to organic growth in line with FY2025's 7%. Cloud growth at or above 15% in H1 2027 would show AI adding to, not substituting, the workflow product; below 10% would suggest the migration tailwind is fading.

FY2026 guidance was raised in August to $50-53M of adjusted EBITDA (from $44-47M) on $516-523M of revenue. H1 delivered $23.2M, so H2 needs $26.8-29.8M; Q3 is guided at $13.5-14.5M.

The cash flow pillar is red because operating cash flow has been negative in every fiscal year. Positive free cash flow in H2 FY2026 (H1 was -$10.2M on FiscalAI's adjusted basis) is the first step to changing that, and the base case assumes ~$15M.

2Q FY2026 free cash flow fell to $130M from $208M a year earlier because Toast bought hardware ahead of memory-price increases (inventory $217M at 30 June 2026 vs $103M a year earlier). Management said conversion of adjusted EBITDA into FCF should improve in the back half. FY2025 FCF was $608M on $633M of adjusted EBITDA (96%). If 2H FY2026 FCF is at least $350M on the ~$415M of implied 2H adjusted EBITDA ($815M guide midpoint less $400M in 1H), the cash thesis holds; if inventory keeps rising, buybacks are being funded from cash.

The CFO said on the 2Q FY2026 call that the P&L impact of memory prices in FY2027 will be greater than in FY2026 because of how inventory is expensed, and management is reinvesting upside into new markets and "long-term bets". The FY2026 guide is ~35% adjusted EBITDA on recurring gross profit ($815M / $2,340M at midpoints). The first FY2027 guide, due with Q4 FY2026 results in February 2027, tells whether operating leverage survives. A guide at or below 35% would push the base-case 30% GAAP EBIT margin on recurring gross profit out by at least a year.

The FY2026 plan is to raise product development to 12–13% of revenue and still lift the adjusted operating margin to ~28.0% (27.5% in FY2025). H1 2026 ran at 11% of revenue with a 29.4% margin, so the step-up lands in H2 2026 and carries into 2027 without the FRR divestment tailwind. Analysts pressed on this three times on the H1 call and management would only say it intends "slight increases on a regular annual basis". Guidance given on February 24, 2027 for another margin increase would confirm the AI spend is self-funding (claim 2); a flat or lower margin guide would break it.

The 2026 buyback was cut to up to €500M (from €1,096M in FY2025) because distributable reserves limit it, not leverage; equity is €940M and net debt/EBITDA 2.0x. The CFO said reserves expand as profits accumulate. At ~€68 (12.5x adjusted EPS) a larger program is the most accretive use of the ~€1.3bn of free cash flow. A 2027 program of €750M or more, announced with FY2026 results, would retire about 5% of the shares at today's price and support claim 3.

PAR sells the operating system of large multi-unit restaurants and convenience stores: PAR POS (Brink), Punchh loyalty, PAR Ordering, Data Central back office and PAR Retail for fuel and c-stores, plus terminals and installation. Subscription revenue was $83.4M in Q2 FY2026, 63% of revenue, and ARR reached $338.0M (+17% YoY, +12.3% organic). Tier-1 rollouts give visibility: Burger King at 400+ sites a month, Papa John's through the end of 2027. The stock fell from $72.67 at FY2024 year end to $13.51 (29 Sep 2026) after an adjusted EBITDA miss in Q4 FY2025 and the 2026 software sell-off, so the platform trades at an EV of about $912M, 2.7x ARR and 1.8x LTM revenue. We are buying an embedded enterprise platform at a hardware-reseller multiple.

Valuation is EV to adjusted EBITDA on FY2029: $672M of revenue ($492M subscription from ~$520M of ARR, $180M of hardware and services held flat) at an 18% adjusted EBITDA margin gives $121M, valued at 12x for an EV of $1,452M. Adjusted EBITDA excludes stock compensation, which ran at 6.0% of LTM revenue; the 12x, against the ~25x the stock trades on LTM adjusted EBITDA, is set low to absorb that. The share count is if-converted: the 4% 2031 notes convert at $19.02, below the target, so 13.9M shares are added and $265M of debt removed, for 57.2M shares. Target $27.60 per share. The return has to come from EBITDA more than tripling, not from the multiple, which compresses.

The return is operating leverage on a cost base reset in 2026. Non-GAAP opex fell from 48% of revenue in Q2 FY2025 to 38% in Q2 FY2026, adjusted EBITDA has risen six quarters in a row to $14.3M, and FY2026 guidance was raised to $50-53M from $44-47M. New platform deals carry two to three products, so ARPU rather than site count drives ARR: organic unique sites fell 2.6% YoY to 145,900 after the planned Punchh exits while organic ARR grew 12.3%. If free cash flow turns sustainably positive from H2 FY2026, net debt of $354M comes down without new equity, and value per share accrues to holders instead of to new issuance, which took the share count from 27.3M at FY2022 to 41.4M.

Organic ARR growth below 10% YoY for two consecutive quarters (it was 11.3% in Q1 FY2026 and 12.3% in Q2 FY2026), or organic unique active sites falling YoY again in any quarter of FY2027 after the 2.6% decline to 145,900 in Q2 FY2026.
FY2027 adjusted EBITDA margin below 12%, non-GAAP opex growing faster than subscription revenue for two quarters, or stock compensation staying above 6% of revenue (6.0% LTM at Q2 FY2026).
Negative free cash flow in FY2027, a new equity raise or new convertible that adds shares, or basic shares above 44M before any conversion of the 2031 notes (41.4M at Q2 FY2026).

Toast is the operating system for US restaurants: point-of-sale software, the hardware it runs on, payments, payroll, lending (Toast Capital) and now AI agents, sold as one integrated platform. At 2Q FY2026 it served ~180,000 locations (+22% yoy, a record 9,500 net adds in the quarter), with $2.41B of ARR (+25%) and $60.7B of quarterly GPV. The economics are a land-and-monetise loop: hardware and installation are sold at a loss (-$259M of gross profit over the last four quarters, ~12% of recurring gross profit) to win a location that then pays a subscription (GAAP subscription gross margin 78% in 2Q FY2026) and a take on every card payment (fintech gross profit ~0.60% of GPV). Recurring gross profit (subscription + fintech, GAAP, FiscalAI) was $2,082M LTM, a 38% 3Y CAGR. We are buying continued share gains in the core SMB restaurant market plus three newer markets (enterprise, international, retail) that management expects to reach ~$200M of ARR in FY2026.

Valuation is anchored to FY2029 GAAP EPS, with stock-based compensation counted as a cost and the tax rate normalised to 20% (hypothesis: the reported rate is ~2% LTM because of loss carryforwards). Base case: ~271K average locations x ~$13.8K of recurring gross profit per location = ~$3.74B of recurring gross profit (18% CAGR from $2,082M LTM, below the current 28%); GAAP operating income at 30% of recurring gross profit (20.7% LTM, 26% in 2Q FY2026) = ~$1.12B; plus ~$60M of interest income, taxed at 20% = ~$946M of net income over 560M diluted shares = $1.69 EPS. At 25x that is ~$42 per share. The stock at $30.46 trades at 39x LTM EPS of $0.78 but ~18x the FY2029 base EPS, so the return has to come from earnings growth while the multiple compresses. Adjusted EBITDA ($739M LTM, company figure) is not the anchor because it excludes ~$237M a year of SBC.

The return comes from operating leverage on a gross-profit base that still compounds above 20%. Operating expenses grew ~19% in 2Q FY2026 against 28% growth in recurring gross profit, and SBC fell from ~14% to ~10% of recurring gross profit in a year. Free cash flow was $576M LTM (FY2025: $608M) with capex of only ~$59M, and the balance sheet carries $1.71B of cash and investments with no financial debt. Management turned that cash on the share count: $486M of buybacks in 1H FY2026 (~19M shares at ~$25.6), cutting diluted shares from 609M (3Q FY2025) to 590M. If EPS compounds from $0.78 LTM to $1.69 in FY2029 and diluted shares reach ~560M, the price return is ~11% a year even with the P/E falling from 39x to 25x. There is no dividend.

Net location adds fall below 6,000 in two consecutive quarters (they were 9,500 in 2Q FY2026 and ~7,000 in 1Q FY2026), or fintech gross profit / GPV drops below 0.55% for two consecutive quarters (0.59% in 2Q FY2026, 0.56% 3Y average), which would show payments pricing being competed away.

GAAP operating income / recurring gross profit falls below 20% for FY2027 (20.7% LTM at 2Q FY2026), or the FY2027 adjusted EBITDA guidance implies a lower margin on recurring gross profit than FY2026 (~35% at the 2Q FY2026 guidance midpoints of $815M / $2,340M), for example because memory costs or new-market spending absorb the leverage.

Diluted weighted shares are above 590M in 4Q FY2027 (590M in 2Q FY2026), or FY2027 free cash flow is below 65% of adjusted EBITDA (FY2025: $608M / $633M = 96%; 2Q FY2026: $130M / $221M = 59% because of the hardware inventory build).

Wolters Kluwer sells embedded professional workflows: CCH Axcess tax software, UpToDate clinical decision support, CT Corporation registered-agent services, enterprise legal spend management and CCH Tagetik. Recurring revenue was 85% of H1 2026 revenue and grew 7% organically; group organic growth was between 5.6% and 6.2% in every year FY2021–FY2025 and the adjusted operating margin rose from 25.3% to 27.5%. The share price fell from €160.40 at the end of FY2024 to about €68 on the fear that generative AI substitutes expert content. The reported numbers have not deteriorated so far: H1 2026 organic growth 5%, recurring cloud software (24% of revenue) +14%, adjusted margin +100bps to 29.4%. The thesis buys that earnings stream at 12.5x LTM adjusted EPS (€5.42).

Valuation is anchored to FY2029 diluted adjusted EPS, the company's own benchmark: revenue from ~€6.2bn (FY2026E) at 5% organic growth to ~€7.2bn, adjusted operating margin 28.5% (FY2026 guidance ~28.0%, while product development rises to 12–13% of revenue), adjusted financing costs of ~€120M, a 24% benchmark tax rate and ~208M diluted shares. That gives ~€7.04 of EPS; at 15x it is ~€105.5 per share. 15x is deliberately below the ~26x the stock averaged at the FY2023–FY2025 year-ends and below RELX (~20x) and Thomson Reuters (~26x) today: part of the AI discount is treated as permanent. Going from 12.5x to 15x adds about 20% to the price; the rest of the return must come from EPS growth, not from a return to the old multiple.

Cash does the compounding. Adjusted free cash flow was €1,348M in FY2025 (22% of revenue, cash conversion 103%) and is guided at €1.30–1.35bn in FY2026 in constant currencies, about a 9% yield on a €15.1bn market cap. Almost all of it goes back to shareholders: a progressive dividend (€2.52 for FY2025) plus buybacks. The binding constraint is not leverage (net debt/EBITDA 2.0x against a 1.5–2.5x policy) but distributable reserves: equity is only €940M after ~€4.1bn of buybacks in FY2022–FY2025, so the 2026 program was cut to €500M from €1.1bn. As profits rebuild reserves the buyback can grow again, and at ~€68 each €500M retires about 3% of the shares.

Group organic growth below 4% in any half-year, or Clinical Solutions organic growth below 3% in two consecutive halves (H1 2026: 5%), or recurring revenue organic growth below 5% (H1 2026: 7%). Any of these would indicate substitution rather than a cyclical dip.

FY2027 guidance (February 2027) calls for an adjusted operating margin below FY2026's ~28.0%, or constant-currency diluted adjusted EPS growth falls below 5% in FY2026 or FY2027: the AI spend would not be self-funding and the EPS path to €7.0 breaks.

Adjusted free cash flow below €1.25bn in FY2026 (guidance €1.30–1.35bn in constant currencies), a 2027 buyback below €500M, or net debt/EBITDA above 2.5x (the top of the policy range) to fund payouts or acquisitions.

174,300 unique sites at Q2 FY2026 (145,900 organic + 28,400 from Bridg, FiscalAI). Growth of ~15% to 200,000 by FY2029 from Tier-1 rollouts (Burger King, Papa John's) and mid-tier wins. No 3Y history: the unique-site count started in Q2 FY2026 and does not bridge to the old Engagement/Operator split.

$338.0M of ARR over 174,300 sites. Rising to ~$2,600 (about 8.7% a year) is in line with the 8% three-year blended ARPU CAGR management cited on the Q2 FY2026 call; organic ARPU rose ~15% YoY in Q2 FY2026 after the low-priced Punchh exits. Bridg sites dilute the average (~$500 each).

200,000 sites x ~$2,600. From an estimated ~$370M at FY2026 year end, that is 12% a year, the low end of management's mid-teens target and with no Tier-1 mega deal. The 41.5% 3Y CAGR (FY2022-FY2025) is mostly acquired (Stuzo, TASK) and is not a guide.
Held near today's level. LTM $183.9M is inflated by a record hardware quarter in Q2 FY2026 ($35.1M, Tier-1 refresh) that management expects to normalize; FY2025 was $164.4M and the 3Y CAGR is flat.
$492M subscription + $180M hardware and services. Against FY2026 guidance of $516-523M that is ~9% a year, with subscription rising to 73% of revenue from 63% in Q2 FY2026.

From 7.25% LTM and ~9.9% implied by FY2026 guidance to 18%. Built bottom-up: ~65% non-GAAP subscription margin on $492M plus ~22% on $180M gives ~$360M of gross profit, less ~$230M of opex (the ~$204M 2026 run-rate growing 4% a year). 3Y average is -3.6% (FY2023 -13.9%, FY2024 -1.8%, FY2025 5.0%).
$672M x 18%. LTM $36.0M (Q3 FY2025 to Q2 FY2026: 5.8 + 7.0 + 8.9 + 14.3). No 3Y CAGR: FY2022 was negative (-$30.5M). This is the company definition, which adds back stock compensation.

Not in the chain, shown because adjusted EBITDA ignores it. $29.6M LTM (5.96%); 3Y average 6.3%. At 4% of $672M it is ~$27M in FY2029, so adjusted EBITDA less stock compensation would be ~$94M, and the 12x on $121M is ~15.5x on that basis.

12x FY2029 adjusted EBITDA. Today EV of $912M is 25.3x LTM adjusted EBITDA and 17.7x the FY2026 guidance midpoint, so the multiple compresses and the return comes from EBITDA. No 3Y average: adjusted EBITDA was negative in FY2023-FY2024.

$353.6M today less ~$216M of cumulative free cash flow H2 FY2026-FY2029 (hypothesis) = ~$138M, less the $265M of 2031 notes treated as converted = -$127M (net cash). History is the FY2023-FY2025 average ($306.5M, $268.0M, $322.2M), per house rule.

41.36M + 13.93M from the 2031 notes (52.5762 shares per $1,000 on $265M) + ~1.9M of net stock-comp dilution (~1.5% a year). The 2030 notes (~$97) and the 2027 stub stay out of the money. 3Y CAGR 14.2% from 27.3M at FY2022 shows how much of past growth was paid in shares.

Implied net income: adj. EBITDA $121.0M − D&A $70.6M (10.5% of revenue) − SBC $26.9M (4% of revenue) = EBIT $23.6M; interest 0 (net cash, no income assumed); pre-tax $23.6M, tax $4.9M (21.0%); FX revaluation 0 → net income $18.6M. Assumptions: SBC at the valuation's SBC % of revenue, D&A 10.5% of revenue (FY2023-25 avg), interest 2.0% on net debt (LTM $8.3M / convertibles $422M), US federal 21% (no tax credit on a loss).

285K locations at the end of FY2029: ~197K at FY2026 year end (1H FY2026 added ~16.5K), then ~31K, ~29K and ~28K net adds, so growth slows from 22% today to ~11% by FY2029. History: 79K at FY2022 to 164K at FY2025, a 3Y CAGR of 27.6%. Average FY2029 locations used for gross profit: ~271K.

~$13.8K of recurring gross profit per average location in FY2029, ~2.5% a year above the $12.7K LTM ($2,082M over ~164K average locations). Mid-single-digit SaaS ARPU growth and new products (ToastIQ Grow, payroll, capital) offset flat GPV per location. History: $10.1K in FY2022 to $12.2K in FY2025, a 3Y CAGR of 6.4%, so the base assumes the per-location gain slows by more than half.

271K average locations x $13.8K = ~$3,740M in FY2029, an ~18% CAGR from $2,082M LTM against 28% growth in 2Q FY2026 and a FY2026 guide of 23–25% (on the company's non-GAAP basis, $2,325–2,355M). GAAP figures from FiscalAI segment data are used throughout; non-GAAP adds back ~$70M a year of SBC and D&A in cost of revenue.

Held at ~0.60% of GPV, the LTM level ($1,282M of fintech gross profit on $214.9B of GPV). The 3Y average is 0.56%, so the base assumes the recent pricing and Toast Capital gains hold but do not keep rising. Each 1bp is ~$30M of gross profit at FY2029 GPV.

30% of recurring gross profit in FY2029 against 20.7% LTM and 26% in 2Q FY2026 (which included a ~$10M tariff refund). Consistent with management's 40%+ long-term adjusted EBITDA margin less ~8% for SBC and ~2% for D&A. Hardware and services gross profit is embedded here at about -10% of recurring gross profit (-12.4% LTM, -14.1% 3Y average).
$3,740M x 30% = ~$1,122M of GAAP operating income, against $431M LTM. SBC is inside this figure as a cost. History is not meaningful as a CAGR: -$384M in FY2022 to $292M in FY2025.

20% normalised rate (hypothesis). The reported rate is ~2.4% LTM ($12M of tax on $498M of pretax income) because of loss carryforwards and a valuation allowance; a release of that allowance or exhaustion of the NOLs moves the book rate toward the statutory ~21–25%. Cash taxes may stay lower than 20% for part of the period.

560M diluted shares in FY2029 against 590M in 2Q FY2026 (diluted weighted average) and 578M basic outstanding. Requires buybacks of roughly $2.7B over 3.5 years to retire ~30M shares net plus ~12M a year of SBC issuance. History: diluted 512M (FY2022) to 607M (FY2025), a 3Y CAGR of +5.8%, so the base assumes the trend reverses as it did in 1H FY2026.

$946M over 560M diluted shares = $1.69, against $0.78 LTM (sum of the last four quarters of diluted EPS). This is a ~2.2x increase over 3.5 years; most of it comes from operating margin, not from volume.

25x for a business growing recurring gross profit ~18% with SBC counted as a cost and no debt. Below the 39x LTM multiple; the 3Y history is not meaningful (negative in FY2023, 1,215x in FY2024, 63x in FY2025). The multiple compresses, so the upside must come from EPS.
$1.69 EPS x 25 x 560M shares = ~$23.6B, or $42.21 per share against $30.46 on 29 September 2026: +39% upside and a 3-year price CAGR of ~11.5%. History: $9.4B at FY2022 to $20.9B at FY2025.
Net cash of ~$2.4B at FY2029: $1,713M today plus ~$3.4B of free cash flow from 2H FY2026 to FY2029, less ~$2.7B of buybacks. The 3Y average is -$1,485M (FY2023–FY2025, house rule: average, not CAGR).

EV of ~$21.2B ($23.6B market cap less $2.4B net cash) on ~$1,202M of GAAP EBITDA ($1,122M EBIT + ~$80M D&A) = 17.7x, or ~14x on company adjusted EBITDA of ~$1.5B (adds back ~$300M of SBC). The current 33.0x is on $482M of LTM GAAP EBITDA (FiscalAI).
~$1,200M of FY2029 free cash flow (~80% of adjusted EBITDA; FY2025 was 96%) on a $23.6B market cap = 5.1%, against 3.3% today ($576M LTM on $17.6B).
